name: paperclip
description: The open-source app everyone uses to manage agents at work
one_liner: A dashboard where you hire a team of AI 'employees' (bots like Claude Code or Codex), give them a business goal, set a budget, and watch them work from your phone.
buyer: A solo founder or small agency owner who wants to run several AI agents on real business tasks (coding, marketing, research) without babysitting a dozen terminal windows.
business_use_cases: A one-person software shop assigns a 'CTO' and 'engineer' agent pair to build and maintain a client's app while the founder just reviews diffs from the dashboard.
A marketing freelancer hires an agent team to run a content pipeline (research, draft, publish) under a fixed weekly budget, then bills the client for oversight.
An agency sells 'managed AI teams' to small businesses: the agency runs Paperclip internally and delivers outcomes (a working app, a marketing calendar) as the product.

money_ideas.idea: A boutique agency that sells outcomes ('we'll build your MVP') produced by an internally-run Paperclip agent team.
A hosted, managed version of Paperclip for non-technical founders who don't want to self-host.
Sell pre-built 'org chart' templates (roles, budgets, skills) for common business goals like 'launch a Shopify store'.

steal_this: Set up a two-agent 'CEO + engineer' rig this weekend on one of your own idle side-project repos, give it a bounded goal and a budget cap, and see what it ships in 48 hours unattended.
